text:
ashok: FYI noticed a latency tail spike in prod after last night's driver bump on our h100 pool. median fine, p95/p99 up ~2.5x for seq=512 workloads.

kyle: ugh, which driver version?

ashok: cuda-driver 542.7 -> 544.2. spike shows up in kernel selection changes for attention path.

maria: any profiling yet? small batches or large? batching heuristics change?

ashok: quick perf dump from the canary VM attached:

```
# profiler summary (shortened)
model: rwd-v2-7b
seq_len: 512
batch: 8
driver: 544.2
kernel picks timeline:
 - t_cross_attention: attn_fused_batched (new, +15% synthetic throughput)
 - t_kv_cache: kv_dense_pack (switched from kv_sparse_pref)
 - matmul: tf32_gemm_xlt (same)
latency summary (ms): median 42 -> 40 (ok), p95 88 -> 210, p99 140 -> 420
```

ashok: The profiler shows a deterministic kernel-path flip at layer 6 depending on seq prefix length. autotuner seems to prefer the fused attention kernel on that driver, but it has worse cache behavior with our KV layout.

jen: do we have traces that show increased DRAM traffic or fallback to non-unified kernels?

ashok: yes, perf counters up for L2 misses and memcpy spikes when kv cache is hot. excerpt from nvprof: 

```
L2_LD_REPLAY: 1.8e8 -> 3.4e8
DRAM_READ_BYTES: 2.1GB -> 7.2GB
kernel: attn_fused_batched   time: 12.2ms  (was attn_split 6.1ms)
```

maria: so the new pick causes extra DRAM churn for our KV layout -> downstream latency. Could be a kernel implementation optimized for different tiling/higher occupancy that thrashes our KV buffer.

kyle: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) force the old kernel via runtime flag/heuristic override; 2) pin driver back in the affected pool; 3) route seq512 traffic to dedicated pool with old driver; 4) deploy micro-patch to autotuner to bias towards kv_sparse_pref.

jen: what's the fastest low-risk action?

ashok: quickest is runtime toggle. we have a flag `RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREFERENCE` that can prefer kernel families per model/seq. i can push a canary config change to prod cluster group B in 10m.

maria: +1. If that buys time we can test a rollback vs autotune patch. rolling back driver across all hosts is higher risk and longer.

infra-bot: deploy-plan for runtime toggle: 
 - target: pool-h100-us-west-b (canary)
 - change: set RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREFERENCE[rwd-v2-7b][seq=512] = "kv_sparse_pref"
 - rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 30m
 - health checks: p95 latency, kernel-choice histogram, DRAM read bytes
 - rollback: automatic on 15% error or >20% p95 regress

kyle: sounds good. also add a trace that logs kernel name per request to S3 for deeper analysis.

ashok: will do. planning the change now. pinging @jen to own post-mortem notes.

jen: I can take the postmortem. please include perf outputs, driver image hashes, and the autotuner seed state. Also we should capture the autotune decision tree snapshot from the canary.

maria: if toggle fixes it, next step is to instrument the autotuner heuristics and add a driver-compatibility weight in scoring. maybe also a tiny evict threshold in KV to avoid thrash for fused kernels.

kyle: when this is stable, we should run a replay test across driver 544.* with our seq distribution to check for other kernel path flips. add a nightly job.

ashok: change applied to pool-h100-us-west-b -> 25% traffic. initial telemetry: p95 dropped from 210 -> 92ms in canary group, DRAM_READ_BYTES down to ~2.4GB. kernel histogram shows reversion to kv_sparse_pref.

maria: great, can you snapshot the autotune state now?

ashok: snapshot saved: s3://redwood-profiles/2141234500-autotune-snapshot.json.gz

infra-bot: rollout progressing to 50% in 10m per plan.

jen: add a short incident note in #incidents referencing this thread. tag customers on Dedicated capacity who might be impacted.

kyle: long-term: add a weighted feature to autotuner that prefers kernel with better kv-locality for models using prefix KV heavily. Also add a post-driver-upgrade smoke harness that runs kernel selection across representative seqs and batches.

maria: agreed. also file followup: run microbench across kernels with our KV alignment change (4KB vs 2KB) — we saw sensitivity in earlier experiments.

ashok: leaving telemetry running and will coordinate rollback of driver only if toggle fails. I’ll post updates here.

jen: thanks. please set a reminder to check in 3 hours and to start incident doc. :thumbsup:

ashok: will do.

infra-bot: rollout reached 100% at 2141234720, health checks passed.

ashok: resolved for now. scheduling replay tests and autotuner patch PR.

jen: noted for postmortem. closing loop later with followups. :white_check_mark:
